interest: Soviet-Japanese border incidents from 1932 denials to 1936 apology.
overview: This file (894.2361) contains U.S. State Department diplomatic correspondence and cross-reference sheets from April 1932 and January 1936 regarding Japanese military border incursions and aircraft flights into the territory of the Soviet Union. Originating from the American Legation in Riga and the American Embassy in Moscow, the records document two distinct episodes along the Soviet-Manchurian frontier. The 1932 documents center on official Soviet press statements in Izvestiya denying foreign reports of clashes and Japanese aerial intrusions near Pogranichnaya, reflecting Moscow's efforts to prevent uncontrolled escalation. The 1936 documents detail the resolution of a serious frontier crisis in which an armed Japanese military reconnaissance aircraft made a forced landing on Soviet territory; following diplomatic exchanges between Soviet Assistant Commissar Boris Stomoniakov and Japanese Ambassador Tamekichi Ohta, the Soviet government agreed to return the plane and wounded pilots after Japan formally expressed regret.
